from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from uuid import uuid4

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import text

from backend.app.application.academy.academy_one_week_workflow import (
    AcademyOneWeekWorkflow,
)
from backend.app.infrastructure.academy.postgresql_academy_notification_repository import (
    PostgreSQLAcademyDeliveryRepository,
    PostgreSQLAcademyUserQuery,
)
from backend.app.infrastructure.persistence.database import (
    create_async_database_engine,
    create_async_session_factory,
)


pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration


class ControlledNotifications:
    """Fail once, then succeed."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls = 0

    @staticmethod
    def is_one_week_eligible(
        *,
        registered_at: datetime,
        now: datetime,
    ) -> bool:
        age = now - registered_at

        return (
            timedelta(days=7)
            <= age
            < timedelta(days=8)
        )

    async def send_one_week(
        self,
        *,
        email: str,
        username: str,
        telegram_chat_id: str | None,
    ) -> dict:
        self.calls += 1

        if self.calls == 1:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "controlled integration failure"
            )

        return {
            "notification_type": "1_WEEK_MILESTONE",
            "email": {
                "status": "mocked",
                "message_id": "retry-integration-message-id",
            },
            "telegram": None,
        }


async def _create_test_user(
    session_factory,
    *,
    user_id,
    email: str,
    username: str,
    created_at: datetime,
) -> None:
    async with session_factory() as session:
        await session.execute(
            text(
                """
                INSERT INTO users (
                    id,
                    email,
                    username,
                    status,
                    trial_status,
                    created_at
                )
                VALUES (
                    :id,
                    :email,
                    :username,
                    'active',
                    'active',
                    :created_at
                )
                """
            ),
            {
                "id": user_id,
                "email": email,
                "username": username,
                "created_at": created_at,
            },
        )

        await session.commit()


async def _delete_test_data(
    session_factory,
    *,
    user_id,
) -> None:
    async with session_factory() as session:
        await session.execute(
            text(
                """
                DELETE FROM academy_notification_deliveries
                WHERE user_id = :user_id
                """
            ),
            {"user_id": user_id},
        )

        await session.execute(
            text(
                """
                DELETE FROM users
                WHERE id = :user_id
                """
            ),
            {"user_id": user_id},
        )

        await session.commit()


async def _get_delivery(
    session_factory,
    *,
    user_id,
):
    async with session_factory() as session:
        result = await session.execute(
            text(
                """
                SELECT
                    status,
                    attempt_count,
                    provider_message_id,
                    last_error,
                    sent_at
                FROM academy_notification_deliveries
                WHERE user_id = :user_id
                  AND notification_type = :notification_type
                """
            ),
            {
                "user_id": user_id,
                "notification_type": (
                    AcademyOneWeekWorkflow.NOTIFICATION_TYPE
                ),
            },
        )

        return result.first()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_real_postgresql_failure_is_persisted_then_retry_succeeds():
    """
    Real PostgreSQL retry lifecycle.

    First run:
        claim -> notification failure -> FAILED

    Second run:
        retry -> notification success -> SUCCEEDED
    """

    engine = create_async_database_engine()
    session_factory = create_async_session_factory(engine)

    user_id = uuid4()

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    created_at = now - timedelta(
        days=7,
        hours=12,
    )

    email = (
        f"academy-retry-{user_id}"
        "@example.invalid"
    )

    username = (
        f"academy_retry_{user_id.hex[:12]}"
    )

    notifications = ControlledNotifications()

    try:
        await _create_test_user(
            session_factory,
            user_id=user_id,
            email=email,
            username=username,
            created_at=created_at,
        )

        workflow = AcademyOneWeekWorkflow(
            users=PostgreSQLAcademyUserQuery(
                session_factory,
            ),
            deliveries=PostgreSQLAcademyDeliveryRepository(
                session_factory,
            ),
            notifications=notifications,
            clock=lambda: now,
        )

        first_result = await workflow.run()

        assert first_result["candidates"] == 1
        assert first_result["attempted"] == 1
        assert first_result["succeeded"] == 0
        assert first_result["failed"] == 1
        assert first_result["skipped"] == 0

        delivery_after_failure = await _get_delivery(
            session_factory,
            user_id=user_id,
        )

        assert delivery_after_failure is not None
        assert delivery_after_failure.status == "FAILED"
        assert delivery_after_failure.attempt_count == 1
        assert (
            delivery_after_failure.provider_message_id
            is None
        )
        assert (
            delivery_after_failure.last_error
            == "controlled integration failure"
        )
        assert delivery_after_failure.sent_at is None

        second_result = await workflow.run()

        assert second_result["candidates"] == 1
        assert second_result["attempted"] == 1
        assert second_result["succeeded"] == 1
        assert second_result["failed"] == 0
        assert second_result["skipped"] == 0

        assert notifications.calls == 2

        delivery_after_retry = await _get_delivery(
            session_factory,
            user_id=user_id,
        )

        assert delivery_after_retry is not None
        assert delivery_after_retry.status == "SUCCEEDED"
        assert delivery_after_retry.attempt_count == 2
        assert (
            delivery_after_retry.provider_message_id
            == "retry-integration-message-id"
        )
        assert delivery_after_retry.last_error is None

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from uuid import uuid4

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import text

from backend.app.application.academy.academy_one_week_workflow import (
    AcademyOneWeekWorkflow,
)
from backend.app.infrastructure.academy.postgresql_academy_notification_repository import (
    PostgreSQLAcademyDeliveryRepository,
    PostgreSQLAcademyUserQuery,
)
from backend.app.infrastructure.persistence.database import (
    create_async_database_engine,
    create_async_session_factory,

pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration


class FakeAcademyNotifications:
    """
    Controlled notification boundary.

    The real Academy workflow executes, but external email and Telegram
    delivery are deliberately replaced by this deterministic test double.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.send_calls: list[dict] = []

    @staticmethod
    def is_one_week_eligible(
        *,
        registered_at: datetime,
        now: datetime,
    ) -> bool:
        if (
            registered_at.tzinfo is None
            or now.tzinfo is None
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "timestamps must be timezone-aware."
            )

        age = now - registered_at

        return (
            timedelta(days=7)
            <= age
            < timedelta(days=8)
        )

    async def send_one_week(
        self,
        *,
        email: str,
        username: str,
        telegram_chat_id: str | None,
    ) -> dict:
        self.send_calls.append(
            {
                "email": email,
                "username": username,
                "telegram_chat_id": telegram_chat_id,
            }
        )

        return {
            "notification_type": "1_WEEK_MILESTONE",
            "email": {
                "status": "mocked",
                "message_id": "integration-test-message-id",
            },
            "telegram": None,
        }


async def _create_test_user(
    session_factory,
    *,
    user_id,
    email: str,
    username: str,
    created_at: datetime,
) -> None:
    """
    Create an isolated user using the authoritative users schema.

    trial_status is required by the production users table and the
    existing Academy persistence tests establish 'active' as the
    valid test value.
    """

    async with session_factory() as session:
        await session.execute(
            text(
                """
                INSERT INTO users (
                    id,
                    email,
                    username,
                    status,
                    trial_status,
                    created_at
                )
                VALUES (
                    :id,
                    :email,
                    :username,
                    'active',
                    'active',
                    :created_at
                )
                """
            ),
            {
                "id": user_id,
                "email": email,
                "username": username,
                "created_at": created_at,
            },
        )

        await session.commit()


async def _delete_test_data(
    session_factory,
    *,
    user_id,
) -> None:
    """
    Remove only records created by this test.
    """

    async with session_factory() as session:
        await session.execute(
            text(
                """
                DELETE FROM academy_notification_deliveries
                WHERE user_id = :user_id
                """
            ),
            {
                "user_id": user_id,
            },
        )

        await session.execute(
            text(
                """
                DELETE FROM users
                WHERE id = :user_id
                """
            ),
            {
                "user_id": user_id,
            },
        )

        await session.commit()


async def _get_delivery(
    session_factory,
    *,
    user_id,
    notification_type: str,
):
    """
    Read the durable delivery record directly from PostgreSQL.
    """

    async with session_factory() as session:
        result = await session.execute(
            text(
                """
                SELECT
                    status,
                    attempt_count,
                    provider_message_id,
                    last_error,
                    sent_at
                FROM academy_notification_deliveries
                WHERE user_id = :user_id
                  AND notification_type = :notification_type
                """
            ),
            {
                "user_id": user_id,
                "notification_type": notification_type,
            },
        )

        return result.first()


def _create_test_database():
    """
    Create the real PostgreSQL engine/session factory.

    DATABASE_URL is resolved by the repository's existing database
    configuration.
    """

    engine = create_async_database_engine()
    session_factory = create_async_session_factory(
        engine,
    )

    return engine, session_factory


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_real_postgresql_academy_workflow_persists_success():
    """
    Execute the real Academy workflow against PostgreSQL.

    Real components:
        PostgreSQLAcademyUserQuery
        PostgreSQLAcademyDeliveryRepository
        AcademyOneWeekWorkflow

    Mocked:
        external notification delivery
    """

    engine, session_factory = _create_test_database()

    user_id = uuid4()

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    created_at = now - timedelta(
        days=7,
        hours=12,
    )

    email = (
        f"academy-integration-{user_id}"
        "@example.invalid"
    )

    username = (
        f"academy_integration_{user_id.hex[:12]}"
    )

    notifications = FakeAcademyNotifications()

    try:
        await _create_test_user(
            session_factory,
            user_id=user_id,
            email=email,
            username=username,
            created_at=created_at,
        )

        workflow = AcademyOneWeekWorkflow(
            users=PostgreSQLAcademyUserQuery(
                session_factory,
            ),
            deliveries=PostgreSQLAcademyDeliveryRepository(
                session_factory,
            ),
            notifications=notifications,
            clock=lambda: now,
        )

        result = await workflow.run()

        assert result["candidates"] == 1
        assert result["attempted"] == 1
        assert result["succeeded"] == 1
        assert result["failed"] == 0
        assert result["skipped"] == 0

        assert len(
            notifications.send_calls,
        ) == 1

        assert (
            notifications.send_calls[0]["email"]
            == email
        )

        assert (
            notifications.send_calls[0]["username"]
            == username
        )

        assert (
            notifications.send_calls[0]["telegram_chat_id"]
            is None
        )

        delivery = await _get_delivery(
            session_factory,
            user_id=user_id,
            notification_type=(
                AcademyOneWeekWorkflow.NOTIFICATION_TYPE
            ),
        )

        assert delivery is not None

        assert delivery.status == "SUCCEEDED"

        assert delivery.attempt_count == 1

        assert (
            delivery.provider_message_id
            == "integration-test-message-id"
        )

        assert delivery.last_error is None

        assert delivery.sent_at is not None

    finally:
        await _delete_test_data(
            session_factory,
            user_id=user_id,
        )

        await engine.dispose()

async def test_real_postgresql_academy_workflow_does_not_reclaim_sent_delivery():
    """
    Execute the real workflow twice.

    First execution:
        claim -> notification -> SUCCEEDED

    Second execution:
        claim rejected -> skipped

    The external notification boundary must therefore be called
    exactly once.
    """

    engine, session_factory = _create_test_database()

    user_id = uuid4()

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    created_at = now - timedelta(
        days=7,
        hours=12,
    )

    email = (
        f"academy-integration-{user_id}"

    )

        f"academy_integration_{user_id.hex[:12]}"
    )

        await _create_test_user(
            session_factory,
            user_id=user_id,
            email=email,
            username=username,
            created_at=created_at,
        )

        workflow = AcademyOneWeekWorkflow(
            users=PostgreSQLAcademyUserQuery(
                session_factory,
            ),
            deliveries=PostgreSQLAcademyDeliveryRepository(
                session_factory,
            ),
            notifications=notifications,
            clock=lambda: now,
        )

        first_result = await workflow.run()

        second_result = await workflow.run()

        assert first_result["candidates"] == 1
        assert first_result["attempted"] == 1
        assert first_result["succeeded"] == 1
        assert first_result["failed"] == 0
        assert first_result["skipped"] == 0

        assert second_result["candidates"] == 1
        assert second_result["attempted"] == 0
        assert second_result["succeeded"] == 0
        assert second_result["failed"] == 0
        assert second_result["skipped"] == 1

        assert len(
            notifications.send_calls,
        ) == 1

        delivery = await _get_delivery(
            session_factory,
            user_id=user_id,
            notification_type=(
                AcademyOneWeekWorkflow.NOTIFICATION_TYPE

        assert delivery.sent_at is not None

            session_factory,

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest

from backend.cybersecurity.scheduler.cybersecurity_scheduler_factory import (
    create_cybersecurity_scheduler_runtime,
)


pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_shared_scheduler_start_registers_academy_and_stops_cleanly():
    """
    Controlled real APScheduler lifecycle smoke test.

    Verifies:
    - one shared scheduler;
    - Academy job registration;
    - existing cybersecurity jobs registration;
    - scheduler starts inside a running asyncio event loop;
    - scheduler becomes running;
    - Academy workflow is not executed;
    - shutdown is invoked cleanly.

    No real email or Telegram delivery is performed.
    """

    academy_workflow = MagicMock(
        name="academy_one_week_workflow",
    )

    runtime = create_cybersecurity_scheduler_runtime(
        workflow_service=MagicMock(
            name="cybersecurity_workflow",
        ),
        academy_one_week_workflow=academy_workflow,
    )

    adapter = runtime.scheduler_adapter

    try:
        adapter.register_jobs()

        jobs = adapter.scheduler.get_jobs()

        job_ids = {
            job.id
            for job in jobs
        }

        assert (
            "academy_one_week_milestone"
            in job_ids
        )

        assert (
            "cybersecurity_daily_report"
            in job_ids
        )

        assert (
            "cybersecurity_weekly_report"
            in job_ids
        )

        assert adapter.scheduler.running is False

        adapter.start()

        assert adapter.scheduler.running is True

        # Starting the scheduler must not execute Academy immediately.
        assert academy_workflow.run.call_count == 0

    finally:
        adapter.shutdown()

        # Give the asyncio scheduler event loop one opportunity to
        # process its shutdown state.
        await asyncio.sleep(0)

    # The important lifecycle contract is that shutdown was invoked
    # and no Academy execution occurred.
    assert academy_workflow.run.call_count == 0

    )

    *,
    state: VoiceCallState,
) -> VoiceCallExecutionContext:
    """
    Create execution context.
    """

    return VoiceCallExecutionContext(
        session=create_session(
            state=state,
        ),
        room=create_room(),
    )

    SpeechProvider,

class FakeSpeechProvider(
    SpeechProvider
):
    """
    Fake speech provider.

    Captures runtime requests.
    """


    def __init__(self):

        self.last_voice_profile = None
        self.last_language_code = None
        self.last_text = None



    def transcribe(
        self,
        audio: bytes,
        language_code: str,
    ) -> str:

        return "bonjour"



    def synthesize(
        self,
        text: str,
        voice_profile: str,
        language_code: str,
    ) -> bytes:

        self.last_text = text

        self.last_voice_profile = (
            voice_profile
        )

        self.last_language_code = (
            language_code
        )

        return b"character-audio"



def create_context() -> InteractionContext:
    """
    Create Yeti interaction context.
    """

    return InteractionContext(
        learner=(
            LearnerContext(
                learner_id="learner-001",
                learning_goals=[
                    "conversation",
                ],
            )
        ),

        world=(
            WorldContext(
                world_id="french_world",
                name="French World",
                language_code="fr",
                available_characters=[
                    "yeti",
                    "alix",
                ],
            )
        ),

        character=(
            CharacterContext(
                character_id="yeti",
                name="Yeti",
                personality_reference=(
                    "storyteller"
                ),
                teaching_style=(
                    "narrative learning"
                ),
            )
        ),

        voice=(
            VoiceContext(
                language_code="fr",
                voice_provider="openai",
                voice_profile="verse",
            )
        ),
    )



def test_character_runtime_generates_character_voice():

    provider = FakeSpeechProvider()


    speech_runtime = VoiceSpeechRuntime(
        speech_provider=provider
    )


    runtime = VoiceCharacterRuntime(
        context=create_context(),
        speech_runtime=speech_runtime,
    )


    audio = runtime.speak(
        "Bonjour, je suis Yeti."
    )


    assert audio == (
        b"character-audio"
    )


    assert runtime.character_id() == (
        "yeti"
    )


    assert provider.last_text == (
        "Bonjour, je suis Yeti."
    )


    assert provider.last_voice_profile == (
        "verse"
    )


    assert provider.last_language_code == (
        "fr"
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest

from backend.app.application.announcement.announcement_publisher import (
    ControlledAnnouncementPublisher,
    PublicationDisabledError,
)
from app.infrastructure.telegram.telegram_announcement_publisher import (
    TelegramAnnouncementPublisher,
)


@dataclass
class FakeTelegramMessage:
    message_id: int


class FakeTelegramClient:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def send_message(
        self,
        *,
        chat_id: str,
        text: str,
        parse_mode: str,
    ) -> FakeTelegramMessage:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "chat_id": chat_id,
                "text": text,
                "parse_mode": parse_mode,
            }
        )
        return FakeTelegramMessage(message_id=42)


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_telegram_publisher_is_thin_adapter():
    client = FakeTelegramClient()

    publisher = TelegramAnnouncementPublisher(
        telegram_client=client,
    )

    message_id = await publisher.publish(
        channel_id="-100123",
        text="Hello",
    )

    assert message_id == "42"
    assert client.calls == [
        {
            "chat_id": "-100123",
            "text": "Hello",
            "parse_mode": "Markdown",
        }
    ]


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_controlled_publisher_blocks_when_disabled():
    client = FakeTelegramClient()

    publisher = ControlledAnnouncementPublisher(
        publisher=TelegramAnnouncementPublisher(
            telegram_client=client,
        ),
        publishing_enabled=False,
    )

    with pytest.raises(PublicationDisabledError):
        await publisher.publish(
            channel_id="-100123",
            text="Hello",
            announcement_type="important",
        )

    assert client.calls == []


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_controlled_publisher_records_success():
    client = FakeTelegramClient()

    publisher = ControlledAnnouncementPublisher(
        publisher=TelegramAnnouncementPublisher(
            telegram_client=client,
        ),
        publishing_enabled=True,
    )

    record = await publisher.publish(
        channel_id="-100123",
        text="Hello",
        announcement_type="important",
    )

    assert record.channel_id == "-100123"
    assert record.message_id == "42"
    assert record.announcement_type == "important"
    assert record.published_at.tzinfo is not None

from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

import pytest

from backend.app.application.announcements.announcement_operations_service import AnnouncementOperationsService
from backend.app.application.announcements.in_memory_repositories import InMemoryAnnouncementRepository, InMemoryPublicationEventRepository
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication_event import PublicationEventType
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication_status import PublicationStatus


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_lifecycle_and_audit_events() -> None:
    service = AnnouncementOperationsService(
        repository=InMemoryAnnouncementRepository(),
        event_repository=InMemoryPublicationEventRepository(),
    )
    item = await service.create(title="Beta 2", body="Release", actor="admin", correlation_id="ann-1")
    assert item.status is PublicationStatus.DRAFT

    await service.mark_ready_for_review(item.id, actor="admin")
    await service.approve(item.id, actor="admin")
    await service.request_publication(item.id, actor="admin")
    await service.mark_published(item.id, actor="admin", provider_message_id="tg-1")

    assert (await service.get(item.id)).status is PublicationStatus.PUBLISHED
    events = await service.audit_log(item.id)
    assert [event.event_type for event in events] == [
        PublicationEventType.CREATED,
        PublicationEventType.READY_FOR_REVIEW,
        PublicationEventType.APPROVED,
        PublicationEventType.PUBLISH_REQUESTED,
        PublicationEventType.PUBLISHED,
    ]
    assert events[-1].provider_message_id == "tg-1"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_failed_publication_is_recorded() -> None:
    service = AnnouncementOperationsService(
        repository=InMemoryAnnouncementRepository(),
        event_repository=InMemoryPublicationEventRepository(),
    )
    item = await service.create(title="Notice", body="Maintenance", actor="admin")
    await service.mark_ready_for_review(item.id, actor="admin")
    await service.approve(item.id, actor="admin")
    await service.request_publication(item.id, actor="admin")
    await service.mark_failed(item.id, actor="admin", error_code="TELEGRAM_TIMEOUT")

    assert (await service.get(item.id)).status is PublicationStatus.FAILED
    events = await service.audit_log(item.id)
    assert events[-1].event_type is PublicationEventType.FAILED
    assert events[-1].error_code == "TELEGRAM_TIMEOUT"


def test_invalid_transition_is_rejected() -> None:
    from backend.app.domain.announcements.announcement import Announcement
    item = Announcement(title="A", body="B", created_by="admin")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        item.mark_published()

FILE: C:\AI Folder\EasyChatBot-Hackathon\backend\tests\announcements\test_ws22_0x_publication_lifecycle_alignment.py
============================================================
from __future__ import annotations

from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication import Publication
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication_status import (
    PublicationStatus,
)
from backend.app.domain.announcements.template_models import (
    PublicationStatus as TemplatePublicationStatus,
    PublicationType,
)


def _publication_type() -> PublicationType:
    """Use an existing publication type without inventing one.

    WS-22.0.x validates lifecycle alignment, not publication-type
    vocabulary.
    """

    members = tuple(PublicationType)

    if not members:
        raise AssertionError(
            "PublicationType must define at least one publication type."
        )

    return members[0]


def _publication() -> Publication:
    return Publication(
        publication_id="ws22-0x-001",
        template_id="beta-release",
        template_version=1,
        publication_type=_publication_type(),
        title="Beta release",
        content="EasyChatBot Beta release announcement.",
    )


def test_ws22_0x_uses_one_canonical_publication_status_enum():
    """The application exposes one PublicationStatus enum."""

    assert PublicationStatus is TemplatePublicationStatus


def test_ws22_0x_canonical_lifecycle():
    """Validate the canonical WS-22 publication lifecycle."""

    publication = _publication()

    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.DRAFT

    publication.request_approval()

    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.PENDING_APPROVAL

    publication.approve()

    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.APPROVED

    publication.begin_publish()

    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.PUBLISHING

    publication.publish_success()

    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.PUBLISHED


def test_ws22_0x_failed_publication_can_retry():
    """A failed publication can return to PUBLISHING."""

    publication = _publication()

    publication.request_approval()
    publication.approve()
    publication.begin_publish()

    publication.mark_failure(
        "publisher unavailable",
    )

    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.FAILED

    assert publication.failure_reason == (
        "publisher unavailable"
    )

    publication.begin_publish()

    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.PUBLISHING


def test_ws22_0x_preserves_legacy_lifecycle_aliases():
    """Existing Announcement Operations vocabulary remains compatible."""

    assert (
        PublicationStatus.READY_FOR_REVIEW
        is PublicationStatus.PENDING_APPROVAL
    )

    assert (
        PublicationStatus.PUBLISH_REQUESTED
        is PublicationStatus.PUBLISHING
    )

    assert (
        PublicationStatus.ARCHIVED
        is PublicationStatus.CANCELLED
    )

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from backend.app.application.announcements.audit import (
    AnnouncementAuditEventType,
    InMemoryAnnouncementAuditSink,
)
from backend.app.application.announcements.publication_service import AnnouncementPublicationService
from backend.app.application.announcements.template_registry import AnnouncementTemplateRegistry
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication import Publication
from backend.app.domain.announcements.template_models import (
    AnnouncementTemplate,
    AnnouncementTemplateVersion,
    PublicationStatus,
    PublicationType,
)
from backend.app.infrastructure.announcements.in_memory_repositories import (
    InMemoryAnnouncementTemplateRepository,
    InMemoryPublicationRepository,
)


def make_template(version: int = 1) -> AnnouncementTemplate:
    tv = AnnouncementTemplateVersion(
        template_id="beta-update",
        version=version,
        publication_type=PublicationType.BETA_UPDATE,
        structure=(
            "ðŸŒ± EasyWorld â€” Growing with You",
            "",
            "BETA UPDATE",
            "",
            "{{title}}",
            "",
            "{{body}}",
            "",
            "{{timing}}",
        ),
        required_fields=frozenset({"title", "body"}),
        optional_fields=frozenset({"timing"}),
    )
    return AnnouncementTemplate(
        template_id="beta-update",
        name="Beta Update",
        publication_type=PublicationType.BETA_UPDATE,
        active_version=version,
        versions=(tv,),
    )


def make_service():
    template_repo = InMemoryAnnouncementTemplateRepository()
    registry = AnnouncementTemplateRegistry(template_repo)
    registry.register(make_template())
    publication_repo = InMemoryPublicationRepository()
    service = AnnouncementPublicationService(
        templates=registry,
        publications=publication_repo,
    )
    return service, registry, publication_repo


def test_required_template_fields_are_enforced():
    _, registry, _ = make_service()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Missing required"):
        registry.preview(template_id="beta-update", values={"title": "X"})


def test_publication_captures_version_and_content_snapshot():
    service, _, repo = make_service()
    publication = service.create(
        publication_id="pub-001",
        template_id="beta-update",
        title="Beta 2",
        values={"title": "Beta 2", "body": "A new beta is available.", "timing": "Today"},
    )
    assert publication.template_id == "beta-update"
    assert publication.template_version == 1
    assert "A new beta is available." in publication.content
    assert repo.get("pub-001").content == publication.content


def test_publication_lifecycle_is_controlled():
    service, _, repo = make_service()
    service.create(
        publication_id="pub-002",
        template_id="beta-update",
        title="Maintenance",
        values={"title": "Maintenance", "body": "Scheduled maintenance."},
    )
    service.request_approval("pub-002")
    service.approve("pub-002")
    service.begin_publish("pub-002")
    service.mark_publish_success("pub-002")
    stored = repo.get("pub-002")
    assert stored.status is PublicationStatus.PUBLISHED
    assert stored.published_at is not None


def test_failed_publication_records_reason():
    service, _, repo = make_service()
    service.create(
        publication_id="pub-003",
        template_id="beta-update",
        title="Announcement",
        values={"title": "Announcement", "body": "Content"},
    )
    service.request_approval("pub-003")
    service.approve("pub-003")
    service.begin_publish("pub-003")
    service.mark_publish_failure("pub-003", "Telegram timeout")
    stored = repo.get("pub-003")
    assert stored.status is PublicationStatus.FAILED
    assert stored.failure_reason == "Telegram timeout"


def test_invalid_transition_is_rejected():
    publication = Publication(
        publication_id="pub-004",

        template_version=1,
        publication_type=PublicationType.BETA_UPDATE,
        title="Test",
        content="Content",
    )
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Invalid publication transition"):
        publication.publish_success()


def test_audit_sink_records_events():
    sink = InMemoryAnnouncementAuditSink()
    sink.record("pub-005", AnnouncementAuditEventType.CREATED)
    sink.record("pub-005", AnnouncementAuditEventType.APPROVED)
    sink.record("pub-005", AnnouncementAuditEventType.PUBLISH_FAILED, "Telegram timeout")
    events = sink.list_for("pub-005")
    assert [e.event_type for e in events] == [
        AnnouncementAuditEventType.CREATED,
        AnnouncementAuditEventType.APPROVED,
        AnnouncementAuditEventType.PUBLISH_FAILED,
    ]
    assert events[-1].details == "Telegram timeout"

def make_editor() -> AnnouncementTemplateEditorService:
    templates = InMemoryAnnouncementTemplateRepository()
    templates.save(
        AnnouncementTemplate(
            template_id="beta-update",
            name="Beta Update",
            publication_type=PublicationType.BETA_UPDATE,
            active_version=2,
            description="Official Beta update pattern.",
            category="Beta",
            versions=(
                AnnouncementTemplateVersion(
                    template_id="beta-update",
                    version=2,
                    publication_type=PublicationType.BETA_UPDATE,
                    structure=(
                        "EASYCHATBOT ACADEMY",
                        "",
                        "{{headline}}",
                        "",
                        "{{body}}",
                        "",
                        "{{timing}}",
                    ),
                    required_fields=frozenset({"headline", "body"}),
                    optional_fields=frozenset({"timing"}),
                ),
            ),
        )
    )

    registry = AnnouncementTemplateRegistry(templates)
    publications = InMemoryPublicationRepository()
    publication_service = AnnouncementPublicationService(
        templates=registry,
        publications=publications,
    )

    return AnnouncementTemplateEditorService(
        templates=registry,
        publications=publication_service,
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from uuid import uuid4

import pytest

from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.contracts import (
    PublicationExecutionRequest,
    PublicationExecutionStatus,
)
from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.publication_execution_service import (
    PublicationExecutionService,
)
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication_status import PublicationStatus


@dataclass
class FakePublication:
    id: object
    title: str = "Beta 2"
    content: str = "Release announcement"
    status: PublicationStatus = PublicationStatus.APPROVED

    def begin_publish(self) -> None:
        self.status = PublicationStatus.PUBLISHING

    def publish_success(self, provider_message_id: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.status = PublicationStatus.PUBLISHED

    def mark_failure(self, reason: str) -> None:
        self.status = PublicationStatus.FAILED


class FakePublisher:
    def __init__(self, message_id: str = "provider-1") -> None:
        self.calls = 0
        self.message_id = message_id

    async def publish(self, **kwargs) -> str:
        self.calls += 1
        return self.message_id


class FailingPublisher:
    async def publish(self, **kwargs) -> str:
        raise RuntimeError("private provider response must not be audited")


class FakeAudit:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.successes = []
        self.failures = []

    async def record_success(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.successes.append(kwargs)

    async def record_failure(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.failures.append(kwargs)


def request(publication_id):
    return PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=publication_id,
        idempotency_key="exec-001",
        actor="admin",
        correlation_id="corr-001",
    )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_approved_publication_executes_and_audits_success():
    publication = FakePublication(uuid4())
    publisher = FakePublisher()
    audit = FakeAudit()
    service = PublicationExecutionService(publisher=publisher, audit=audit)

    result = await service.execute(
        publication=publication,
        request=request(publication.id),
    )

    assert result.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
    assert result.provider_message_id == "provider-1"
    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.PUBLISHED
    assert publisher.calls == 1
    assert len(audit.successes) == 1
    assert audit.successes[0]["provider_message_id"] == "provider-1"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_same_idempotency_key_does_not_publish_twice():
    publication = FakePublication(uuid4())
    publisher = FakePublisher()
    audit = FakeAudit()
    service = PublicationExecutionService(publisher=publisher, audit=audit)
    first = request(publication.id)

    result_one = await service.execute(publication=publication, request=first)
    result_two = await service.execute(
        publication=publication,
        request=first,
    )

    assert result_one.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
    assert result_two.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY
    assert publisher.calls == 1
    assert len(audit.successes) == 1


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_non_approved_publication_is_rejected_before_publish():
    publication = FakePublication(uuid4(), status=PublicationStatus.DRAFT)
    publisher = FakePublisher()
    audit = FakeAudit()
    service = PublicationExecutionService(publisher=publisher, audit=audit)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="approved"):
        await service.execute(
            publication=publication,
            request=request(publication.id),
        )

    assert publisher.calls == 0
    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.DRAFT
    assert audit.successes == []
    assert audit.failures == []


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_publisher_failure_updates_lifecycle_and_audits_stable_error_code():
    publication = FakePublication(uuid4())
    audit = FakeAudit()
    service = PublicationExecutionService(
        publisher=FailingPublisher(),
        audit=audit,
    )

    result = await service.execute(
        publication=publication,
        request=request(publication.id),
    )

    assert result.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.FAILED
    assert result.error_code == "RUNTIMEERROR"
    assert publication.status is PublicationStatus.FAILED
    assert len(audit.failures) == 1
    assert audit.failures[0]["error_code"] == "RUNTIMEERROR"
    assert "private provider response" not in str(audit.failures).lower()

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from uuid import uuid4

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import delete
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import (
    AsyncSession,
    async_sessionmaker,
    create_async_engine,
)

from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.contracts import (
    PublicationExecutionRequest,
    PublicationExecutionStatus,
)
from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_contracts import (
    DurableExecutionStatus,
)
from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_execution_service import (
    DurablePublicationExecutionService,

from backend.app.infrastructure.announcements.sqlalchemy_publication_execution_repository import (

def _async_database_url() -> str:
    value = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL")

    if not value:
        pytest.skip(
            "DATABASE_URL is not configured for PostgreSQL integration tests."
        )

    if value.startswith("postgresql+asyncpg://"):
        return value

    if value.startswith("postgresql://"):
        return value.replace(
            "postgresql://",
            "postgresql+asyncpg://",
            1,
        )

    pytest.skip("DATABASE_URL is not a PostgreSQL URL.")


def _create_database():
    """
    Create the existing PostgreSQL connection infrastructure for this
    integration test.

    No pytest fixture is involved.
    """

    engine = create_async_engine(
        _async_database_url(),
        pool_pre_ping=True,
    )

    session_factory = async_sessionmaker(
        engine,
        class_=AsyncSession,
        expire_on_commit=False,
    )

    return engine, session_factory


class RecordingPublisher:
    """Test-only provider boundary."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        result: str = "provider-message-1",
        fail: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self.result = result
        self.fail = fail
        self.calls: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    async def publish(self, **kwargs) -> str:
        self.calls.append(kwargs)

        if self.fail:
            error = RuntimeError(
                "simulated provider timeout"
            )
            error.error_code = "PROVIDER_TIMEOUT"
            raise error

        return self.result


class RecordingAudit:
    """Test-only implementation of the existing audit contract."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.successes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        self.failures: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    async def record_success(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.successes.append(kwargs)

    async def record_failure(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.failures.append(kwargs)


@dataclass
class ApprovedPublication:
    """Minimal publication test double."""

    id: object
    title: str = "Beta release"
    content: str = "EasyChatBot Beta release."
    status: str = "approved"

    def begin_publish(self) -> None:
        self.status = "publishing"

    def publish_success(
        self,
        provider_message_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.status = "published"

    def mark_failure(
        self,
        error_code: str,
    ) -> None:
        self.status = "failed"


async def _delete_execution(
    session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession],
    key: str,
) -> None:
    """Delete only the execution record created by the test."""

    async with session_factory() as session:
        await session.execute(
            delete(
                PublicationExecutionRecordModel
            ).where(
                PublicationExecutionRecordModel.idempotency_key
                == key
            )
        )

        await session.commit()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_success_survives_new_repository_and_service_instance() -> None:
    """
    Verify:

    1. Execution persists in PostgreSQL.
    2. A new repository/service instance can recover it.
    3. Duplicate execution is detected after restart.
    4. Provider message ID survives restart.
    5. Correlation ID survives restart.
    6. Provider is not called twice.
    """

    engine, session_factory = _create_database()

    key = f"ws22-3-2x1-success-{uuid4()}"
    publication_id = uuid4()
    correlation_id = f"corr-{uuid4()}"

    try:
        # ---------------------------------------------------------
        # Application instance #1
        # ---------------------------------------------------------

        publisher_1 = RecordingPublisher(
            result="provider-message-123"
        )

        audit_1 = RecordingAudit()

        repository_1 = (
            SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository(
                session_factory
            )
        )

        service_1 = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
            publisher=publisher_1,
            execution_repository=repository_1,
            audit=audit_1,
        )

        request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            idempotency_key=key,
            correlation_id=correlation_id,
            actor="integration-test",
        )

        publication = ApprovedPublication(
            id=publication_id
        )

        result = await service_1.execute(
            publication=publication,
            request=request,
        )

        assert result.status is (
            PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
        )

        assert result.provider_message_id == (
            "provider-message-123"
        )

        assert len(publisher_1.calls) == 1
        assert len(audit_1.successes) == 1

        # ---------------------------------------------------------
        # Simulated application restart
        # ---------------------------------------------------------

        publisher_2 = RecordingPublisher(
            result="SHOULD-NOT-BE-SENT"
        )

        audit_2 = RecordingAudit()

        repository_2 = (
            SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository(
                session_factory
            )
        )

        service_2 = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
            publisher=publisher_2,
            execution_repository=repository_2,
            audit=audit_2,
        )

        replay = await service_2.execute(
            publication=ApprovedPublication(
                id=publication_id
            ),
            request=request,
        )

        assert replay.status is (
            PublicationExecutionStatus.IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY
        )

        assert replay.provider_message_id == (
            "provider-message-123"
        )

        # Critical guarantee.
        assert publisher_2.calls == []

        # Replay must not generate another success audit.
        assert audit_2.successes == []

        # ---------------------------------------------------------
        # Verify PostgreSQL persistence
        # ---------------------------------------------------------

        persisted = (
            await repository_2.get_by_idempotency_key(
                key
            )
        )

        assert persisted is not None

        assert persisted.status is (
            DurableExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
        )

        assert persisted.publication_id == (
            publication_id
        )

        assert persisted.idempotency_key == key

        assert persisted.correlation_id == (
            correlation_id
        )

        assert persisted.attempt == 1

        assert persisted.provider_message_id == (
            "provider-message-123"
        )

        assert persisted.error_code is None

    finally:
        await _delete_execution(
            session_factory,
            key,
        )

        await engine.dispose()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_failure_survives_restart_and_remains_retryable() -> None:
    """
    Verify:

    1. Failure persists in PostgreSQL.
    2. Failure survives a new repository instance.
    3. Error code persists.
    4. Correlation ID persists.
    5. Failed execution can be retried.
    6. Successful retry persists.
    """

    engine, session_factory = _create_database()

    key = f"ws22-3-2x1-failure-{uuid4()}"
    publication_id = uuid4()
    correlation_id = f"corr-{uuid4()}"

    request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=publication_id,
        idempotency_key=key,
        correlation_id=correlation_id,
        actor="integration-test",
    )

    try:
        # ---------------------------------------------------------
        # Initial execution â€” failure
        # ---------------------------------------------------------

        repository_1 = (
            SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository(
                session_factory
            )
        )

        publisher_1 = RecordingPublisher(
            fail=True
        )

        audit_1 = RecordingAudit()

        service_1 = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
            publisher=publisher_1,
            execution_repository=repository_1,
            audit=audit_1,
        )

        result = await service_1.execute(
            publication=ApprovedPublication(
                id=publication_id
            ),
            request=request,
        )

        assert result.status is (
            PublicationExecutionStatus.FAILED
        )

        assert result.error_code == (
            "PROVIDER_TIMEOUT"
        )

        assert len(publisher_1.calls) == 1
        assert len(audit_1.failures) == 1

        # ---------------------------------------------------------
        # Simulated restart
        # ---------------------------------------------------------

        repository_2 = (
            SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository(
                session_factory
            )
        )

        persisted = (
            await repository_2.get_by_idempotency_key(
                key
            )
        )

        assert persisted is not None

        assert persisted.status is (
            DurableExecutionStatus.FAILED
        )

        assert persisted.publication_id == (
            publication_id
        )

        assert persisted.correlation_id == (
            correlation_id
        )

        assert persisted.attempt == 1

        assert persisted.error_code == (
            "PROVIDER_TIMEOUT"
        )

        assert persisted.provider_message_id is None

        # ---------------------------------------------------------
        # Retry
        # ---------------------------------------------------------

        publisher_2 = RecordingPublisher(
            result="provider-after-retry"
        )

        audit_2 = RecordingAudit()

        service_2 = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
            publisher=publisher_2,
            execution_repository=repository_2,
            audit=audit_2,
        )

        retry = await service_2.execute(
            publication=ApprovedPublication(
                id=publication_id
            ),
            request=request,
        )

        assert retry.status is (
            PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
        )

        assert retry.provider_message_id == (
            "provider-after-retry"
        )

        assert len(publisher_2.calls) == 1
        assert len(audit_2.successes) == 1

        # ---------------------------------------------------------
        # Verify final PostgreSQL state
        # ---------------------------------------------------------

        persisted_after_retry = (
            await repository_2.get_by_idempotency_key(
                key
            )
        )

        assert persisted_after_retry is not None

        assert persisted_after_retry.status is (
            DurableExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
        )

        assert (
            persisted_after_retry.provider_message_id
            == "provider-after-retry"
        )

        assert (
            persisted_after_retry.correlation_id
            == correlation_id
        )

        assert (
            persisted_after_retry.publication_id
            == publication_id
        )

    finally:
        await _delete_execution(
            session_factory,
            key,
        )

        await engine.dispose()

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from uuid import uuid4

import pytest

from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.contracts import (
    PublicationExecutionRequest,
    PublicationExecutionStatus,
)
from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_contracts import (
    DurableExecutionStatus,
)
from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_execution_service import (
    DurablePublicationExecutionService,
)
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication_status import PublicationStatus


@dataclass
class Publication:
    id: object
    status: PublicationStatus = PublicationStatus.APPROVED
    title: str = "Beta 2"
    content: str = "Release"

    def begin_publish(self):
        self.status = PublicationStatus.PUBLISHING

    def publish_success(self, provider_message_id=None):
        self.status = PublicationStatus.PUBLISHED

    def mark_failure(self, reason):
        self.status = PublicationStatus.FAILED


@dataclass
class Record:
    publication_id: object
    idempotency_key: str
    correlation_id: str
    attempt: int
    status: DurableExecutionStatus
    provider_message_id: str | None = None
    error_code: str | None = None


class DurableFakeRepository:
    """Persists state in a shared object, simulating a restart."""

    def __init__(self, store=None):
        self.store = store if store is not None else {}

    async def get_by_idempotency_key(self, key):
        return self.store.get(key)

    async def create_started(self, *, publication_id, idempotency_key, correlation_id):
        if idempotency_key in self.store:
            raise RuntimeError("duplicate idempotency key")
        record = Record(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
            correlation_id=correlation_id,
            attempt=1,
            status=DurableExecutionStatus.STARTED,
        )
        self.store[idempotency_key] = record
        return record

    async def mark_succeeded(self, *, idempotency_key, provider_message_id):
        record = self.store[idempotency_key]
        record.status = DurableExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
        record.provider_message_id = provider_message_id
        return record

    async def mark_failed(self, *, idempotency_key, error_code):
        record = self.store[idempotency_key]
        record.status = DurableExecutionStatus.FAILED
        record.error_code = error_code
        return record


class Publisher:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = 0

    async def publish(self, **kwargs):
        self.calls += 1
        return "telegram-independent-provider-id"


class Audit:
    def __init__(self):
        self.success = []
        self.failure = []

    async def record_success(self, **kwargs):
        self.success.append(kwargs)

    async def record_failure(self, **kwargs):
        self.failure.append(kwargs)


def req(pid):
    return PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=pid,
        idempotency_key="durable-001",
        actor="admin",
        correlation_id="corr-001",
    )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_duplicate_is_detected_after_service_restart():
    store = {}
    publisher = Publisher()
    audit = Audit()
    publication = Publication(uuid4())

    service_one = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
        publisher=publisher,
        execution_repository=DurableFakeRepository(store),
        audit=audit,
    )
    first = await service_one.execute(
        publication=publication,
        request=req(publication.id),
    )

    # New service instance: no in-memory idempotency state survives here.
    service_two = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
        publisher=publisher,
        execution_repository=DurableFakeRepository(store),

    assert publisher.calls == 1

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from uuid import uuid4

import pytest

    PublicationExecutionRequest,
    PublicationExecutionStatus,
)

)

)

@dataclass
class FakeTelegramMessage:
    message_id: int


class FakeTelegramClient:
    """Deterministic Telegram transport test double."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[dict[str, str]] = []

    async def send_message(
        self,
        *,
        chat_id: str,
        text: str,
        parse_mode: str,
    ) -> FakeTelegramMessage:
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "chat_id": chat_id,
                "text": text,
                "parse_mode": parse_mode,
            }
        )

        return FakeTelegramMessage(message_id=9001)


class InMemoryExecutionRepository:
    """Minimal durable repository double for the integration test."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.records = {}

    async def get_by_idempotency_key(self, idempotency_key: str):
        return self.records.get(idempotency_key)

    async def create_started(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id,
        idempotency_key,
        correlation_id,
    ):
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_contracts import (
            DurableExecutionStatus,
            PublicationExecutionRecord,
        )

        existing = self.records.get(idempotency_key)

        if existing is not None:
            return existing

        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

        record = PublicationExecutionRecord(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
            correlation_id=correlation_id,
            attempt=1,
            status=DurableExecutionStatus.STARTED,
            provider_message_id=None,
            error_code=None,
            created_at=now,
            updated_at=now,
        )

        self.records[idempotency_key] = record
        return record

    async def mark_succeeded(
        self,
        *,
        idempotency_key,
        provider_message_id,
    ):
        from dataclasses import replace
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_contracts import (
            DurableExecutionStatus,
        )

        record = self.records[idempotency_key]

        updated = replace(
            record,
            status=DurableExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED,
            provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
            error_code=None,
            updated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )

        self.records[idempotency_key] = updated
        return updated

    async def mark_failed(
        self,
        *,
        idempotency_key,
        error_code,
    ):
        from dataclasses import replace
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_contracts import (
            DurableExecutionStatus,
        )

        record = self.records[idempotency_key]

        updated = replace(
            record,
            status=DurableExecutionStatus.FAILED,
            error_code=error_code,
            updated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )

        self.records[idempotency_key] = updated
        return updated


class RecordingAudit:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.successes: list[dict] = []
        self.failures: list[dict] = []

    async def record_success(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.successes.append(kwargs)

    async def record_failure(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.failures.append(kwargs)


@dataclass
class ApprovedPublication:
    id: object
    title: str = "Beta 2"
    content: str = "EasyChatBot Beta 2 is available."
    status: str = "approved"

    def begin_publish(self) -> None:
        pass

    def publish_success(
        self,
        provider_message_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.status = "published"

    def mark_failure(self, error_code: str) -> None:
        self.status = "failed"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ws22_3_3_executes_through_telegram_adapter() -> None:
    telegram_client = FakeTelegramClient()

    telegram_publisher = TelegramAnnouncementPublisher(
        telegram_client=telegram_client,
    )

    bridge = LegacyAnnouncementPublisherBridge(
        publisher=telegram_publisher,
        channel_id="-100123456789",
    )

    repository = InMemoryExecutionRepository()
    audit = RecordingAudit()

    service = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
        publisher=bridge,
        execution_repository=repository,
        audit=audit,
    )

    publication_id = uuid4()

    request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=publication_id,
        idempotency_key=f"ws22-3-3-{uuid4()}",
        actor="integration-test",
        correlation_id=f"corr-{uuid4()}",
    )

    publication = ApprovedPublication(
        id=publication_id,
    )

    result = await service.execute(
        publication=publication,
        request=request,
    )

    assert result.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
    assert result.provider_message_id == "9001"

    assert len(telegram_client.calls) == 1
    assert telegram_client.calls[0] == {
        "chat_id": "-100123456789",
        "text": (
            "Beta 2\n\n"
            "EasyChatBot Beta 2 is available."
        ),
        "parse_mode": "Markdown",
    }

    persisted = await repository.get_by_idempotency_key(
        request.idempotency_key
    )

    assert persisted is not None
    assert persisted.provider_message_id == "9001"
    assert persisted.correlation_id == request.correlation_id
    assert persisted.publication_id == publication_id

    assert len(audit.successes) == 1
    assert audit.successes[0]["publication_id"] == publication_id
    assert audit.successes[0]["actor"] == "integration-test"
    assert (
        audit.successes[0]["correlation_id"]
        == request.correlation_id
    )
    assert (
        audit.successes[0]["provider_message_id"]
        == "9001"
    )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ws22_3_3_idempotency_prevents_second_telegram_send() -> None:
    telegram_client = FakeTelegramClient()

    telegram_publisher = TelegramAnnouncementPublisher(
        telegram_client=telegram_client,
    )

    bridge = LegacyAnnouncementPublisherBridge(
        publisher=telegram_publisher,
        channel_id="-100123456789",
    )

    repository = InMemoryExecutionRepository()
    audit = RecordingAudit()

    service = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
        publisher=bridge,
        execution_repository=repository,
        audit=audit,
    )

    publication_id = uuid4()

    request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=publication_id,
        idempotency_key=f"ws22-3-3-idempotent-{uuid4()}",
        actor="integration-test",
        correlation_id=f"corr-{uuid4()}",
    )

    first = await service.execute(
        publication=ApprovedPublication(id=publication_id),
        request=request,
    )

    second = await service.execute(
        publication=ApprovedPublication(id=publication_id),
        request=request,
    )

    assert first.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED

    assert (
        second.status
        is PublicationExecutionStatus.IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY
    )

    assert second.provider_message_id == "9001"

    # Critical WS-22 guarantee:
    # the provider receives exactly one publication.
    assert len(telegram_client.calls) == 1

    # Only the original successful execution records an audit success.
    assert len(audit.successes) == 1

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

import pytest
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from sqlalchemy import delete
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import (
    AsyncSession,
    async_sessionmaker,
    create_async_engine,
)

from backend.app.infrastructure.announcements.publication_audit_repository import (
    PublicationAuditEventModel,
    SqlAlchemyPublicationAuditRepository,
)


def _load_repository_environment() -> None:
    """Load the repository root .env for integration tests."""

    repository_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
    env_file = repository_root / ".env"

    load_dotenv(env_file, override=False)


def _database_url() -> str:
    _load_repository_environment()

    value = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL")

    if not value:
        pytest.fail(
            "DATABASE_URL is not available after loading the repository .env."
        )

    if value.startswith("postgresql+asyncpg://"):
        return value

    if value.startswith("postgresql://"):
        return value.replace(
            "postgresql://",
            "postgresql+asyncpg://",
            1,
        )

    pytest.fail("DATABASE_URL is not a PostgreSQL URL.")


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_success_audit_survives_new_repository_instance() -> None:
    engine = create_async_engine(
        _database_url(),
        pool_pre_ping=True,
    )

    session_factory = async_sessionmaker(
        engine,
        class_=AsyncSession,
        expire_on_commit=False,
    )

    publication_id = uuid4()

    try:
        repository_1 = SqlAlchemyPublicationAuditRepository(
            session_factory
        )

        await repository_1.record_success(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            actor="integration-test",
            correlation_id="corr-success",
            provider_message_id="provider-123",
        )

        # Simulated application restart:
        # create a completely new repository instance.
        repository_2 = SqlAlchemyPublicationAuditRepository(
            session_factory
        )

        events = await repository_2.list_for(publication_id)

        assert len(events) == 1

        event = events[0]

        assert event.publication_id == str(publication_id)
        assert event.event_type == "published"
        assert event.actor == "integration-test"
        assert event.correlation_id == "corr-success"
        assert event.provider_message_id == "provider-123"
        assert event.error_code is None
        assert event.occurred_at is not None

    finally:
        async with session_factory() as session:
            await session.execute(
                delete(PublicationAuditEventModel).where(
                    PublicationAuditEventModel.publication_id
                    == str(publication_id)
                )
            )
            await session.commit()

        await engine.dispose()

from __future__ import annotations

def _require_database_url() -> None:
    from dotenv import load_dotenv

    load_dotenv()

    import os

    if not os.getenv("DATABASE_URL"):
        pytest.skip(
            "DATABASE_URL is not configured for PostgreSQL integration tests."
        )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_shared_async_persistence_factory_uses_canonical_base() -> None:
    """Verify WS-22 repositories use the canonical persistence boundary."""

    _require_database_url()

    engine = create_async_database_engine()
    session_factory = create_async_session_factory(engine)

    try:
        assert engine is not None
        assert session_factory is not None

        # Both WS-22 models must belong to the canonical platform metadata.
        assert (
            PublicationExecutionRecordModel.metadata
            is Base.metadata
        )
        assert (
            PublicationAuditEventModel.metadata
            is Base.metadata
        )

        # The repositories must accept the canonical async factory.
        execution_repository = SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository(
            session_factory
        )
        audit_repository = SqlAlchemyPublicationAuditRepository(
            session_factory
        )

        assert execution_repository is not None
        assert audit_repository is not None

    finally:
        await engine.dispose()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_shared_async_session_reaches_same_postgresql_database() -> None:
    """Verify the canonical async factory can execute against PostgreSQL."""

    _require_database_url()

    engine = create_async_database_engine()
    session_factory = create_async_session_factory(engine)

    try:
        async with session_factory() as session:
            result = await session.execute(select(1))
            assert result.scalar_one() == 1

    finally:
        await engine.dispose()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_execution_and_audit_repositories_share_same_session_boundary() -> None:
    """Verify execution and audit repositories use the same injected factory."""

    _require_database_url()

    engine = create_async_database_engine()
    session_factory = create_async_session_factory(engine)

    try:
        execution_repository = SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository(
            session_factory
        )
        audit_repository = SqlAlchemyPublicationAuditRepository(
            session_factory
        )

        # The important architectural assertion is that both adapters receive
        # the same canonical session factory rather than creating their own.
        assert execution_repository._session_factory is session_factory
        assert audit_repository._session_factory is session_factory

    finally:
        await engine.dispose()

        publisher=RecordingPublisher(),
    )

    try:
        assert isinstance(
            composition,
            DurablePublicationExecutionComposition,
        )

        assert isinstance(
            composition.service,
            DurablePublicationExecutionService,
        )

        assert isinstance(
            composition.execution_repository,
            SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository,
        )

        assert isinstance(
            composition.audit_repository,
            SqlAlchemyPublicationAuditRepository,
        )

        assert isinstance(
            composition.audit,
            DurablePublicationExecutionAudit,
        )

        # Critical architectural invariant:
        # both WS-22 durable repositories use the canonical shared
        # async session factory.
        assert (
            composition.execution_repository._session_factory
            is composition.session_factory
        )

        assert (
            composition.audit_repository._session_factory
            is composition.session_factory
        )

    finally:
        await composition.dispose()

        )

class RecordingPublisher:

        self.calls.append(kwargs)

async def _cleanup(
    composition,
    *,
    idempotency_key: str,
    publication_id: UUID,

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_composition_executes_and_persists_execution_and_audit() -> None:
    _load_repository_environment()

    publisher = RecordingPublisher()

    composition = create_durable_publication_execution_composition(
        publisher=publisher,
    )

    publication_id = uuid4()
    idempotency_key = f"ws22-3-5-4-{uuid4()}"
    correlation_id = f"corr-{uuid4()}"

    request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=publication_id,
        idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
        actor="ws22-3-5-4-test",
        correlation_id=correlation_id,
    )

    publication = ApprovedPublication(id=publication_id)

    try:
        result = await composition.service.execute(
            publication=publication,
            request=request,
        )

        assert result.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
        assert result.provider_message_id == "provider-ws22-3-5-4-001"
        assert len(publisher.calls) == 1

        async with composition.session_factory() as session:
            execution = await session.scalar(
                select(PublicationExecutionRecordModel).where(
                    PublicationExecutionRecordModel.idempotency_key
                    == idempotency_key
                )
            )

            assert execution is not None
            assert execution.idempotency_key == idempotency_key
            assert execution.correlation_id == correlation_id
            assert execution.provider_message_id == (
                "provider-ws22-3-5-4-001"
            )

            audit_events = (
                await session.scalars(
                    select(PublicationAuditEventModel)
                    .where(
                        PublicationAuditEventModel.publication_id
                        == str(publication_id)
                    )
                    .order_by(PublicationAuditEventModel.id)
                )
            ).all()

            assert len(audit_events) == 1
            assert audit_events[0].event_type == "published"
            assert audit_events[0].actor == "ws22-3-5-4-test"
            assert audit_events[0].correlation_id == correlation_id
            assert audit_events[0].provider_message_id == (
                "provider-ws22-3-5-4-001"
            )

    finally:
        await _cleanup(
            composition,
            idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
            publication_id=publication_id,
        )
        await composition.dispose()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_composition_replays_without_second_provider_call() -> None:
    _load_repository_environment()

    publisher = RecordingPublisher()

    composition = create_durable_publication_execution_composition(
        publisher=publisher,
    )

    publication_id = uuid4()
    idempotency_key = f"ws22-3-5-4-replay-{uuid4()}"
    correlation_id = f"corr-{uuid4()}"

    request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=publication_id,
        idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
        actor="ws22-3-5-4-test",
        correlation_id=correlation_id,
    )

    try:
        first = await composition.service.execute(
            publication=ApprovedPublication(id=publication_id),
            request=request,
        )

        second = await composition.service.execute(
            publication=ApprovedPublication(id=publication_id),
            request=request,
        )

        assert first.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
        assert second.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY

        assert second.provider_message_id == first.provider_message_id
        assert len(publisher.calls) == 1

    finally:
        await _cleanup(
            composition,
            idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
            publication_id=publication_id,
        )
        await composition.dispose()

class RecordingPublisher:
    def __init__(self, *, fail: bool = False) -> None:
        self.fail = fail
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    async def publish(self, **kwargs) -> str:
        self.calls.append(kwargs)

        if self.fail:
            error = RuntimeError("simulated provider timeout")
            error.error_code = "PROVIDER_TIMEOUT"
            raise error

        return "provider-ws22-3-5-5-retry-success"


@dataclass

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_failure_is_durable_and_retry_succeeds() -> None:
    _load_repository_environment()

    publication_id = uuid4()
    idempotency_key = f"ws22-3-5-5-{uuid4()}"
    correlation_id = f"corr-{uuid4()}"

    request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
        publication_id=publication_id,
        idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
        actor="ws22-3-5-5-test",
        correlation_id=correlation_id,
    )

    composition_1 = create_durable_publication_execution_composition(
        publisher=RecordingPublisher(fail=True),
    )

    try:
        failed = await composition_1.service.execute(
            publication=ApprovedPublication(id=publication_id),
            request=request,
        )

        assert failed.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.FAILED
        assert failed.error_code == "PROVIDER_TIMEOUT"

        async with composition_1.session_factory() as session:
            execution = await session.scalar(
                select(PublicationExecutionRecordModel).where(
                    PublicationExecutionRecordModel.idempotency_key
                    == idempotency_key
                )
            )

            assert execution is not None
            assert execution.status == "failed"
            assert execution.attempt == 1
            assert execution.error_code == "PROVIDER_TIMEOUT"
            assert execution.provider_message_id is None

            audit_events = (
                await session.scalars(
                    select(PublicationAuditEventModel)
                    .where(
                        PublicationAuditEventModel.publication_id
                        == str(publication_id)
                    )
                    .order_by(PublicationAuditEventModel.id)
                )
            ).all()

            assert len(audit_events) == 1
            assert audit_events[0].event_type == "publish_failed"
            assert audit_events[0].error_code == "PROVIDER_TIMEOUT"
            assert audit_events[0].correlation_id == correlation_id

    finally:
        await composition_1.dispose()

    # Simulate application restart: completely new composition.
    publisher_2 = RecordingPublisher(fail=False)

    composition_2 = create_durable_publication_execution_composition(
        publisher=publisher_2,
    )

    try:
        retry = await composition_2.service.execute(
            publication=ApprovedPublication(id=publication_id),
            request=request,
        )

        assert retry.status is PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
        assert retry.provider_message_id == (
            "provider-ws22-3-5-5-retry-success"
        )
        assert len(publisher_2.calls) == 1

        async with composition_2.session_factory() as session:
            execution = await session.scalar(
                select(PublicationExecutionRecordModel).where(
                    PublicationExecutionRecordModel.idempotency_key
                    == idempotency_key
                )
            )

            assert execution is not None
            assert execution.status == "succeeded"
            assert execution.attempt == 2
            assert execution.error_code is None
            assert execution.provider_message_id == (
                "provider-ws22-3-5-5-retry-success"
            )

            audit_events = (
                await session.scalars(
                    select(PublicationAuditEventModel)
                    .where(
                        PublicationAuditEventModel.publication_id
                        == str(publication_id)
                    )
                    .order_by(PublicationAuditEventModel.id)
                )
            ).all()

            assert len(audit_events) == 2
            assert audit_events[0].event_type == "publish_failed"
            assert audit_events[1].event_type == "published"

    finally:
        await _cleanup(
            composition_2,
            idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
            publication_id=publication_id,
        )
        await composition_2.dispose()

class RecordingPublisher:
